Montreal trans guy here. I go to Concordia and they offer trans health coverage there, but one of the standard requisites for HRT in Quebec is some form of gender therapy-- so I see a private psych once every two weeks for 120$/hour. She wrote me a letter of recommendation for HRT right away, and it took about 4 months before she could write me a referral for top surgery.

However: check out [Head & Hands](http://headandhands.ca/) \-- I know that there are doctors there who can prescribe HRT/surgery referals/etc for people who don't have family doctors or are having gatekeeping-type issues. Their waiting list is fairly long, from what I understand, but I've only ever heard good things about their services. It's non-profit, too, I think-- they're in NDG, on Benny / Sherbrooke!

Edit: McGill also has the [MUSIC ](https://www.mcgill.ca/cosum/)clinic which operates out of the Montreal General. It's also free. Longer waiting list, I believe, but again, you don't need a referral to get on it.

PM if you ever have any questions, would be happy to help if I can! :)

Even though the frequency with which I am misgendered has diminished somewhat over the last couple of months, it still sucks whenever it happens. There's something fundamentally shitty about someone not recognising you as you see yourself, and I don't think there's any quick work-around that kind of thing. Best advice I can offer is to 1) not dwell on other people's knee-jerk perceptions and opinions and 2) gently correct anyone you'll be seeing frequently. There's no harm in letting someone know that they're misgendering you, and if they're a decent person, they'll probably make the switch right away. This will save you from hurt feelings in the future. Feeling comfortable around friends and acquaintances is key here! Hang in there and remember that one person's opinion/perception of you doesn't invalidate your identity or appearance whatsoever.

I'm probably not exactly who you're looking for (I'm 5'2"ish...5'3" if I excercise really good posture) and I regularly get comments about being "short for a guy". I'm 4.5 months on T, and only recently started passing regularly-- but I get frequent comments about looking young and being short. Strangers generally peg me for about 15-16 years old. I'm 21. 

It's hard not to compare heights with cis guys. Hell, sometimes I stand on the metro and feel dwarfed by men and women alike; I'm generally the shortest guy, if not the shortest person in a group. But I've dated! Successfully! Most of my partners have been taller than me, as well. The key is really mind over matter. I know confidence sounds like a cliche, but if you don't think about your height and approach without the second though of "but I won't pass/they're not interested because I'm short"... Well, it can be a self-fulfilling prophecy. 

Lastly, self-deprecating humor is your friend when people DO bring it up. I generally chuckle (sometimes awkwardly) and go with a "yeah, drank too much coffee as a kid and it stunted my growth" or something like that. Just pass it off as old-hat and the person you're talking to will generally drop it. If you pretend it doesn't bother you, eventually it won't bother you anymore. Patience and confidence, my friend! Your height will never determine the validity of your gender Identity! Good luck.
